IQ playback / recordiq_playback, iq_record, iq_stop, iq_status, ul-rct-testPlay a stored waveform (ETM) on antennas, capture ADC samples, on-target UL conformance test
CW tonearm_cw_playback, activate_playback_recording, stop_cw_playbackSingle tone from the FPGA CW generator (see CWGEN01)
Attenuation / gainset-dac-atten, set-adc-atten, set-dac-current, set-dac-input-gain, set-dfe-ch-gain, set-pre-cfr-gainTrim analog and digital levels per DAC/ADC/antenna
NCOset-nco-freq, set-nco-switchShift a converter NCO by an offset in Hz; toggling vs static NCO switch
Calibration / RSSIarm_iq_recording, calibration, get-rssiOBS/RX/TX calibration capture; per-ADC dBFS and dBm
RFFE / PA / LNAset-rffe-switch-state, set-column-switch-state, mb-modify-pa/lna/rffe, mb-get-pa/lnaPath routing and amplifier enables via the midboard
RF-GPIO (debug)set/get-rf-gpio, rf-gpio-tdd-override, rf-gpio-tx-rx-abcdDrive TX/RX/bypass lines directly, bypassing TDD
AGCagc-ctrl, agc-reload-config, get-agc-rssiEnable/hold AGC, reload tuning live, on-demand RSSI
Level 2 — the commands you actually type
IQ playback and recording. iq_playback <file> <ant 0-7 | 255 = all> <transfers, 0 = continuous> <flags> streams a stored waveform through the iq_dma driver (/dev/iq_dma0); iq_status shows what is playing and iq_stop ends it. iq_record <file> <ant> <packet size> captures one antenna; the old delay/threshold arguments are still parsed but ignored. Keep waveform files on the persistent data partition so a firmware update does not wipe them. ul-rct-test <test> <frc> <bw> <ant> <frames> (list with -l) runs the on-target UL conformance test; it shares the IQ path, so it cannot run alongside a recording or RF sensing.
CLI:/> iq_playback /data/etm/nr_tm3p1_100M.binlt;data-partition/data/etm/nr_tm3p1_100M.bingt;/etm.bin 255 0 0   # all antennas, continuous
CLI:/> iq_status
CLI:/> get-rssi                                        # adc_dbfs and dBm per ADC
CLI:/> iq_stop
Attenuation and gain. Attenuation is in 0.1 dB units, so 10 = 1 dB.
CommandArgumentsNotes
set-dac-atten / set-adc-atten<idx> <0.1 dB units>DAC 0–7, ADC 0–9. DAC atten goes through operations_manager: needs an active carrier, refused if Dynamic-Vdd owns the DAC
set-dac-current<idx> <µA>e.g. 15000; full-scale current (see DACG01)
set-dfe-ch-gain<ch> <16-bit>0x161 for SCS 15 kHz with PA and for SCS 30 kHz; 0x100 for SCS 15 kHz without PA
set-pre-cfr-gain<cc 0/1>Digital gain ahead of CFR, per component carrier
set-dac-input-gain1A..2D <val> | --all 4|8Band is positional (1 = first band, 2 = second), never the real band number
set-atten-dfe / get-atten-dfe—Retired stubs (GRDEV-8885); they print the replacement command
NCO. set-nco-freq <0 dac | 1 adc> <idx> <Hz offset> shifts a converter NCO; set-nco-switch <col> <0 toggling | 2 static>. See FPLAN01 for how the NCO value itself is derived.
Calibration and RSSI. arm_iq_recording <adc 0-9> + activate_playback_recording arm a synchronised tone/capture; calibration <1 obs | 2 rx | 3 tx> <amplitude> <write phase>; get-rssi prints adc_dbfs and RSSI in dBm per ADC (see RSSI02).
RFFE routing. set-rffe-switch-state <rffe> <col> <band> <pol> <state> with states Oper 0, ObsDnD 1, TxDnD 2, RxDnD 3, ObsCal 4, TxCal 5, RxCal 6; set-column-switch-state uses oper 0, cal_obs 1, cal_rx 2, cal_tx 3. mb-modify-pa / mb-modify-lna <en> <ant> <band> and mb-get-pa / mb-get-lna switch and read the amplifiers (this is what FC20 uses to isolate one RFFE).
AGC. agc-ctrl [<inst> enable|disable|static]; agc-reload-config re-reads the personality agc-config live without a restart; get-agc-rssi <inst> <ch> shows dBFS, LUT index, lambda, RX gain and dBm at the port. "AGC not present in bitstream (agc_com=0)" means the loaded FPGA image has no AGC block.
Level 2 — manual TX/RX by RF-GPIO (B41 example, GRDEV-7950)
On TDD units the TX/RX/LNA-bypass lines are normally driven by the TDD engine. For bench work you can take them over. Bit 31 of the RF-GPIO word is the TDD mux: 1 = TDD engine drives the pins, 0 = the register value drives them.
CLI:/> rf-gpio-tdd-override off          # bit31 = 0: register now owns the pins
CLI:/> rf-gpio-tx-rx-abcd b41 1 ABCD tx  # computes and writes the full word
CLI:/> get-rf-gpio 1                     # read back
   ... measure ...
CLI:/> rf-gpio-tx-rx-abcd default        # 0x80000020: hand back to TDD
B41 grp1 wordMeaning
0x000010A5RX only
0x00000F62TX only, LNAs bypassed
0x00000F20TX only, LNAs not bypassed
0x80000020Default: TDD engine in control (hand-back value)
set-rf-gpio <grp> <32-bit> overwrites the whole word (including bit 31 and the PA-enable bits); rf-gpio-tdd-override is a read-modify-write of bit 31 only; rf-gpio-tx-rx-abcd <flavour> <band> <AB|CD|ABCD> <rx|tx|rx&tx|rxbyp|rxbyp&tx> holds a polarity-aware bit table for each flavour (b7, lb, b1b3, b41, n78, b3b7, b4b7), writes the full word and preserves bit 31. See B41T for the TDD trigger timing these lines normally follow.
Level 3 — pitfalls and real cases
  • The tdd-override trap. "Override off" is the setting that gives you control (bit 31 = 0). After any TDD pattern has been applied, bit 31 is 1: your write reads back perfectly, yet the pins do not move. Always run rf-gpio-tdd-override off first.
  • Wrong hand-back word. An older procedure handed back with 0x80000000. That clears bit 5 and resets the midboard. The correct value is 0x80000020.
  • Cross-process write race. operations_manager and fault_manager also write the RF-GPIO words and DAC attenuation (GRDEV-4729, GRDEV-7975). A carrier reconfigure or a fault can silently undo a CLI setting, so re-read before you measure.
  • Second band without a carrier. set-dac-input-gain 2x touches the second-band DFE. With no active carrier on that band the access bus-aborts and the watchdog resets the unit.
  • "All antennas" played on one. An old iq_playback bug stored "all" (33) in a 5-bit field, giving bitmap 0x02, so only one antenna transmitted. Fixed; if per-antenna power looks lopsided on old firmware, suspect it. Recording always takes a single antenna.
  • Input flushed. The line reader flushes anything received before the prompt returns. Scripted drivers must wait for CLI:/> before sending the next line. Done that way, a 187-combination RF-GPIO sweep ran with no failures.
  • Power-up glitch. PL outputs float for about 1 s before the bitstream loads (PA enable high, reset low). The breakout board H3 header exposes the GRP1 bits if you need to scope this.
  • Variant differences. On the 5-band AAU, mb-get-rffe-temperature/current/alarms take an extra <band 1/3/8/20/28/41>; the PA/LNA antenna argument means A–D; mb-modify-rffe uses rffe 1–4 and pol 1–4.
  • Removed commands. Phase-shifter commands (set/get-phase-shifter-state, column phase) disappeared with cal_manager and now return "command not found"; phase work moved to the phase-cal verbs (PHCAL01).
  • 2026 behaviour changes that break old scripts: the *-usleep-tx-* commands gained a band argument (USLEEP01); mb-upgrade-firmware now leaves PA/LNA disabled; switch-state read-back now matches what was written; the DPD kill state was retired (DPD02).
Interview Q&A
Q: You write a B41 TX-only word to RF-GPIO, it reads back correctly, but the analyzer shows nothing changed. Why?
A: Bit 31 (TDD mux) is still 1, so the TDD engine owns the pins and the register value is ignored. Run rf-gpio-tdd-override off first, then write the word.
Q: Why were dedicated CLI commands added instead of keeping mw.l/md.l scripts?
A: The 2026.2 FPGA register refactor moved addresses and broke every hard-coded poke. The commands resolve addresses from CSR-generated defines, so they survive future refactors.
Q: set-dac-atten 3 25 — what attenuation, and why might it be refused?
A: 2.5 dB on DAC 3 (0.1 dB units). It routes through operations_manager, so it needs an active carrier and is refused if Dynamic-Vdd currently owns the DAC.
Q: What value hands RF-GPIO back to the TDD engine on B41, and what goes wrong with 0x80000000?
A: 0x80000020. 0x80000000 also clears bit 5, which resets the midboard.
Q: Your script sends ten CLI lines back-to-back and only some take effect. What is happening?
A: The CLI line reader flushes input that arrives before it re-prompts. Send each line only after seeing CLI:/>.
CWGEN01 CW Tone Generator (cw_gen / CORDIC) — FCW maths, run modes, legacy vs LUT-NCO design, CLI and register use, two-tone tests RCT click to expand ▾
In plain English
Sometimes you do not want a modulated LTE/NR carrier at all — you want one clean sine wave at a known frequency and level. The FPGA has a small block for exactly that, the CW generator (module tx_calibration inside dl_top, often called cw_gen). Inside is a CORDIC / NCO: a phase accumulator that adds a fixed step every clock and turns the phase into a sine and cosine. The tone is injected into the TX chain of one DAC channel, so you can measure a TX path with a spectrum analyzer, compare phases between parallel paths for phase calibration (PHCAL01/PHCAL02), or combine two tones for an intermodulation test. You set three things: frequency (as a phase-increment word), amplitude (in DAC counts) and run mode.
Where the tone is injected
The only thing that changes the maths between designs is the sample rate f_s that the phase accumulator runs at.
Level 1 — registers and run modes
OffsetRegisterContent
0x00tx_ctrlbit0 cordic_start, bit1 cordic_cont, bit2 cordic_repetitive (new), bits[6:4] ch_sel = DAC 0–7
0x04cordic_iq_dataamplitude: I field [15:0] in signed DAC counts (full scale 0x7FFF); Q field unused in the new design
0x08cordic_freq32-bit frequency control word (FCW), a phase increment, not Hz
0x0Cduration_txburst length in DPD-clock sample beats
0x10dpd_sample_rateread-only, new design only: the f_s of this variant in Hz
Mode bitLegacy behaviourNew (LUT-NCO) behaviour
cordic_startrepeating burstsstrictly one-shot: one frame-aligned burst, then stops
cordic_contre-fired fixed bursts under the hoodtruly continuous, no phase reset, not frame-aligned, duration ignored; runs until cleared
cordic_repetitive—frame-aligned burst from phase 0 every frame (duration capped at 10 ms) = the old "start" behaviour
Set exactly one mode bit; if several are set the priority is cont > repetitive > start. Phase calibration uses cont: a phase measurement needs a tone whose phase never jumps during or between captures.
Level 2 — the three numbers, and how to drive it
Frequency word. FCW = round(f_tone / f_s × 2^32) and back again f_tone = FCW / 2^32 × f_s. Resolution is f_s / 2^32 (about 0.06 Hz at 245.76 MHz); the range is ±f_s/2; negative offsets are written as 32-bit two's complement. At 245.76 MHz: +5 MHz → 87,381,333 = 0x05355555; −5 MHz → 0xFACAAAAB.
Amplitude. counts = round(32767 × 10^(dBFS/20)): −20 dBFS → 3277, −6 dBFS → 16422. Only the I field is used in the new design.
Duration. round(10 ms × f_s) beats for a one-frame burst. Legacy reset value 2457599 = 10 ms at 245.76 MHz. Ignored in continuous mode.
CLI path (preferred) — the new firmware takes the offset in MHz and computes the FCW itself from the live f_s, logging both:
CLI:/> arm_cw_playback 1 5 3277        # DAC 1, +5 MHz offset, -20 dBFS, default mode 0 = continuous
CLI:/> activate_playback_recording       # tone on
CLI:/> stop_cw_playback                  # zero amplitude, clear start/cont/repetitive

# optional 4th argument: 0 continuous | 1 every frame (repetitive) | 2 one-shot
# offset may be negative or fractional, e.g. -2.5
Direct registers (sweeps, or with cli-manager stopped). Load amplitude and frequency first, enable last; stop by clearing tx_ctrl, then the amplitude:
md.l <base>+0x10 1          # read dpd_sample_rate FIRST (new design)
mw.l <base>+0x04 0x0CCD     # amplitude 3277 (-20 dBFS)
mw.l <base>+0x08 0x<fcw>   # computed against THIS f_s
mw.l <base>+0x00 0x02       # ch_sel=0, cordic_cont -> ON   (0x12 = ch_sel 1 + cont)
mw.l <base>+0x00 0x0        # stop
mw.l <base>+0x04 0x0
Two-tone tests. Arm two DAC channels (or two tones combined externally) at offsets ±Δf around the carrier centre with equal amplitude; IM3 products then appear at ±3Δf. Back each tone off by 6 dB relative to a single-tone level so the summed peak stays below full scale (see IMD2CC01 and DPD02 for what IM3 tells you).
Level 3 — pitfalls and the design change
  • The f_s trap. The legacy design always ran at 245.76 MHz, so people kept tables of hand-computed FCWs. The new LUT-NCO design (GRDEV-8003, B0103 and peer variants) runs at the per-variant DPD rate. A word computed for 245.76 MHz on a variant whose DPD rate is, say, 491.52 MHz puts the tone at twice the intended offset. The CLI path reads 0x10 and is self-correcting; a direct poke is not.
  • Transcription drift. An old legacy example used 87415930 for +5 MHz; the correct word is 87381333 — an error of about 2 kHz, enough to miss a narrow capture window. Compute words, never copy them.
  • Mode semantics changed. Legacy "start" repeated every frame; new "start" fires once. Scripts that relied on the old behaviour must switch to repetitive. Legacy "cont" re-fired bursts (and so reset phase); only the new "cont" is phase-continuous.
  • No carrier, no tone. With no TX carrier active, arm_cw_playback reports success but nothing is transmitted — every capture reads zeros (PHCAL01).
  • PA safety. A complex CW tone has a constant envelope (no crest factor), so at the same peak counts it carries far more average power than OFDM, all in one bin. Keep amplitude modest (calibration flows cap it at 10000 counts with any PA on) and use an attenuator at the analyzer.
  • Why post-DPD is better. Pre-CFR, a strong tone could be clipped by CFR and then pre-distorted by a DPD that had adapted to OFDM statistics, so you measured CFR/DPD artefacts rather than the path. Post-DPD, the tone sees only interpolation, DAC and the analog chain, and the block uses less PL area.
Interview Q&A
Q: Compute the FCW for a −5 MHz tone at f_s = 245.76 MHz.
A: +5 MHz is round(5/245.76 × 2^32) = 87,381,333 = 0x05355555. Negative is the two's complement: 2^32 − 87,381,333 = 0xFACAAAAB.
Q: Which run mode do you use for phase calibration and why?
A: cordic_cont: in the new design it is truly continuous with no phase reset, so every capture sees the same tone phase reference.
Q: You poke a hand-computed FCW on a B0103 unit and the tone is not where you expect. What did you miss?
A: The new design runs at the variant's DPD rate, not 245.76 MHz. Read dpd_sample_rate at offset 0x10 and recompute, or use arm_cw_playback with the offset in MHz.
Q: What amplitude counts give −12 dBFS?
A: 32767 × 10^(−12/20) ≈ 32767 × 0.251 ≈ 8231.
Q: Why was the CW generator moved after CFR/DPD?
A: So the tone is not clipped by CFR or distorted by DPD coefficients trained on OFDM; it measures the real path from DAC onwards, and the LUT-NCO uses less logic.
PHCAL01 Reference Phase Calibration of a 5-band AAU — OBS → TX → RX, routes, dwell, commit and the phase-offset LUT RCT click to expand ▾
In plain English
A 5-band AAU drives each antenna column from one DAC, but the signal is split to four RF front-end boards (RFFEs) on B1/B3/B41, or two on low band. Each board's TX, RX and observation (OBS) path has its own cable lengths, filters and amplifiers, so each has its own insertion phase. If the four copies arrive at the radiating elements with different phases they do not add up coherently and the beam loses gain. Reference phase calibration measures every path against a reference board using a CW tone (CWGEN01), and writes one correction per path into a phase-offset LUT on the midboard; the phase shifters then apply it. The measurement maths is in PHCAL02; this card is the procedure, routing and storage.
Calibration order and what is being aligned
TX is captured at the observation receiver through each board's shared OBS shifter; RX is captured at the RX ADC and does not pass the OBS shifter.
Level 1 — core facts
  • Order OBS → TX → RX is mandatory. TX is observed through each board's OBS phase shifter (PS_Obs), so an OBS change shifts every TX reading; OBS must be pinned first. RX does not pass PS_Obs (a 60° OBS change moved RX by at most 0.6°).
  • Path naming: each column (one DAC) is split 4 ways on B1/B3/B41 and 2 ways on low band, so a path is identified by band, column and RFFE together.
  • Switch encodings: an SPDT is one-hot (C1 C2) and 00 terminates; an SP4T uses throws 100/011/010/001 and 111 terminates. Clearing AUTO_OBS_ENABLE (bit 0) gives manual routing, and it must be set again afterwards or the observation path stays dark in normal operation (breaking DPD).
  • The LUT: one 24-byte block per RFFE = 12 × int16 little-endian degrees: slots 0–3 TX, 4–7 RX, 8–11 OBS. Primary blocks at 0x01E0 + 24k, the B3 block at 0x0240 + 24k. Write the whole block in one transaction (separate 2-byte writes revert each other); the write is live immediately.
  • Shifter resolution: the read-back is the nearest shifter step — within 1° on midband and B41, within 3° on low band.
  • Factory data is precious: the LUT holds each board's factory offsets and nothing else keeps a copy. Dump it before you touch it.
BandConverter facts that matter
B1 / B3 (midband)Run and commit each band separately. OBS injects on the band's B lane (only that lane has the cal coupler). RX tone offset B1 −107.5 MHz, B3 +95.0 MHz
B41All four columns on DAC 0–3, DPD 0, ORX 8 — an ORX 9 capture is noise. OBS is one ABCD route per board, so it resolves boards, not columns. RX tone at 0 MHz offset
B8 / B20B28 (low band)Each column spans two boards. OBS injects on one DAC for every column (retuned for B8). Zeroing one low band also zeroes the shared RX shifter slots. RX tone B8 −108.0 MHz
Level 2 — a calibration session, one band at a time
The phase-cal verbs live in cli-manager (RUCLI01) and exist only on the 5-band AAU. Run from a session that will not drop: cli-manager exits when its client disconnects, and in the middle of a zero-first run that leaves the band's offsets at 0.
CLI:/> phase-cal-verify-unit                 # VERDICT: READY on every board
CLI:/> get-ptp-lock-state                    # LOCKED
   (activate the band carriers via the running datastore - every PA comes on)
CLI:/> mb-set-mode 1 0                       # calibration mode; mb-get-mode 0 -> Calibration
CLI:/> phase-cal-verify-switches ALL         # optional: every switch takes every code
CLI:/> phase-cal-commit zero <band> dry-run   # SAVE THIS: prints current (factory) offsets
CLI:/> phase-cal-deltas ALL <band> ALL       # zero-first + obs-first; prints results file
CLI:/> phase-cal-commit <results.json> dry-run
CLI:/> phase-cal-commit <results.json>       # or OBS|TX|RX; logs each old block first
CLI:/> phase-cal-deltas ALL <band> ALL false # residual over the new offsets: ~0 per lane
CLI:/> phase-cal-restore-defaults            # clears route bits, AUTO_OBS_ENABLE back on
CLI:/> mb-set-mode 0 0
What phase-cal-deltas does per cell: parks the DPD dwell, applies the route, turns off every PA of the measured band and of the band feeding the tone (and checks they really are off), enables only the column under test for TX, arms the CW tone, captures, estimates phase (PHCAL02), then restores switches, tone, dwell and B41 direction bits. The PAs are left off — re-activate the carriers or reboot to go back on air.
Commit rules: commit refuses TX if the OBS offsets it would leave differ from the ones TX was measured through, so commit OBS and TX together from the same ALL file. A board that read "not measurable" leaves unmeasured slots, and commit refuses that stage; commit only the stages that measured (e.g. phase-cal-commit <file> RX). Commits write one board at a time with no rollback; each old block goes to the debug log, and phase-cal-write-block puts it back.
SymptomCauseFix
refused: midboard not in calibration modemode 0mb-set-mode 1 0
no board measuredroute dark, or tone not armedphase-cal-show-route for the same path; check stage and band
one midband board never measuresboard with no firmware accepts writes and does nothingphase-cal-verify-unit names it (GRDEV-9364)
cells drop out at randomrelays still moving at capture startsettle time should read 50 ms; never below 20
OBS path stays dark after the sessionAUTO_OBS_ENABLE left 0phase-cal-restore-defaults in calibration mode
Level 3 — how it is built, traps and real findings
Routes are generated, not hand-written. A switch bit map plus a truth table in YAML go through tools/cal/encode_cal_bitmaps.py into a committed generated_cal_bitmaps.h, checked by validate_cal_bitmaps.py. The design principle is target as instrument, host as brains: the RU only routes, plays and captures; the analysis and decisions live in host-side code.

The DPD dwell skip-mask. DPD cycles its observation receiver between its 4 ports; for a capture it must be parked on the port under test. set-dpd-skip-port takes a bitmap of ports to skip: portmap = (2^p − 1) − 2^port, i.e. 15 − 2^port (port 0 → 14, port 3 → 7). Passing the port number instead parks every other port and leaves the measured one live — it still looks like a valid measurement. After an interrupted run also run set-dpd-skip-port 1 0, because restore-defaults unparks only DPD 0.

  • Stale-route trap: activating carriers takes the midboard out of calibration mode. If you do not re-enter it, apply-route writes nothing and the capture measures the previous route — a plausible but wrong number. phase-cal-get-switch-state catches it.
  • Safety: never arm CW by hand above amplitude 10000 with a PA on (the deltas verb caps TX there). With no TX carrier, arm_cw_playback "succeeds" but transmits nothing and every capture reads zeros.
  • Encoder bug: early routes read SPDTs C2-first, which inverted every route; fixed in the encoder. Two sheet values were also wrong on B41: TX SW7 = 111 measured −30 dB versus +19.5 dB for 110, and RX SW9 011 had to be 110. Measure a route before trusting a spreadsheet.
  • B41 direction: the verb clears the TDD mux bit itself; by hand, run rf-gpio-tdd-override off first (RUCLI01). A spur near +95 MHz, 36–37 dB over the median, appears on B41 captures even with no CW — compare against a tone-off capture.
  • Open issues: on midband RX aligns after a commit (board spread 118° → ≤16°) but TX does not; RFFE3/4 sit 37–55° from RFFE1/2 as a pair; B1 OBS is about 17 dB weaker than B3 OBS. PHCAL02 shows the antenna-level proof.
Interview Q&A
Q: Why must OBS be calibrated before TX?
A: TX is measured at the observation receiver through each board's OBS phase shifter, so any OBS offset adds to the TX reading. Pin OBS first; RX does not pass the OBS shifter.
Q: What is in one RFFE's LUT block and how must it be written?
A: 24 bytes = 12 int16 LE degree values: TX slots 0–3, RX 4–7, OBS 8–11. Write the whole block in one transaction; separate 2-byte writes revert each other.
Q: You want to park the DPD dwell on port 2. What portmap?
A: 15 − 2^2 = 11. Passing 2 would skip only port 1 and leave the measured port cycling.
Q: Calibration results look reasonable but never change when you change the route. What happened?
A: Activating the carriers dropped calibration mode, so apply-route wrote nothing and you measured a stale route. Re-enter mb-set-mode 1 0 and confirm with phase-cal-get-switch-state.
Q: What must you save before the first commit, and why?
A: The current LUT (phase-cal-commit zero <band> dry-run). It holds factory offsets that exist nowhere else, and commits have no rollback.
PHCAL02 Phase-Calibration Measurement Science — single-tone phase estimation, frequency search, SNR gate, start-time ambiguity, repeatability and combining gain RCT click to expand ▾
In plain English
PHCAL01 tells you which path to measure; this card is about how a phase is pulled out of a capture and how far you can trust it. You record a few hundred thousand IQ samples of a CW tone. The raw samples spin round the circle thousands of times, so their average is zero and the phase is hidden. Multiply every sample by a replica spinning the opposite way at exactly the tone frequency: the tone stops rotating and becomes one fixed vector A·ejφ, while the noise keeps spinning and averages away. The angle of that vector is the path phase. Everything else — finding the exact frequency, rejecting DC, gating on SNR, the capture-start ambiguity — is about making that one number honest.
Stopping the rotation
Signal adds coherently (proportional to N), noise incoherently (proportional to the square root of N), which is where the 10log10(N) processing gain comes from.
Level 1 — the estimator
  • Joint tone + DC fit. Rather than a plain single-bin DFT, the code minimises Σ|x[k] − A·ejωk − D|² over A and D. That is a 2×2 complex least-squares system (the Gram matrix of the tone basis and the constant), solved in closed form with Cramer's rule. When the tone sits exactly on a bin the coupling term is zero and it reduces to the DFT; off-bin it removes the DC / LO-leakage that would otherwise tilt φ.
  • Outputs: |A| (amplitude), φ = atan2 of A (the phase at sample 0), residual RMS (what one tone plus DC cannot explain) and SNR = 20·log10(|A| / residual).
  • Processing gain = 10·log10(N).
  • Precision floor σφ ≈ 1/√(2·SNR) (SNR as a linear coherent ratio). At ~52 dB that is about 0.1°: the estimator is never the bottleneck.
Samples NDuration at 245.76 MS/sProcessing gain
24,576100 µs43.9 dB
163,8400.667 ms52.1 dB
245,7601.000 ms53.9 dB
Finding ω. |A|² versus frequency has a main lobe and sidelobes, so a pure golden-section search could settle on a sidelobe. The code first grid-scans at half-bin steps inside ±30 bins of the frequency hint and takes the global peak, then golden-section-refines within ±1 bin to minimise the residual.
Level 2 — making the number honest on the bench
Absolute phase is not real; differences are. φ is referenced to sample 0. If the recorder arms n0 samples late, the result gains 360·f·n0/fs degrees that have nothing to do with the path. iq_record is frame-synced, which removes the large offset, but the latch still wanders by a few samples (measured −2…+1). That is why:
CW offset fdeg per ADC sample at 245.76 MS/sdeg per sample at 61.44 MS/s (RX)
100 Hz0.000150.0006
100 kHz0.1460.586
1 MHz1.465.86
40.54 MHz59.4—
Three separate captures of one +40.54 MHz tone gave identical amplitude and SNR but phases of +130°, −166° and −108° — about 4 samples of arm jitter × 59.4°/sample. At 100 kHz the same jitter costs about 0.4°. Fixes, in order of strength: take a difference between boards under one held tone (phase-cal-deltas — the common start-time rotation cancels) > frame-sync + per-frame CW mode > a low offset. More samples do nothing for this error. Re-arming the tone per column resets the reference, so only phases measured under one tone are comparable.

The two SNRs. phase-cal-measure reports a per-sample SNR (tone amplitude vs broadband residual), not the per-bin peak height a spectrum plot shows: SNRtone ≈ SNRper-bin − 10·log10(nfft). A tone that looks 34 dB above the floor on a 4096-point PSD is about −2 dB per sample. A real low-band capture had tone RMS 4.80 counts against noise 4.63 counts = 0.3 dB and was rightly rejected: the fix is more level, not a bigger FFT.

The SNR gate is now 10 dB (it was 30, then 12). Note that phase-cal-measure still gates at 12 dB until a deltas run or phase-cal-snr-gate has run in that cli-manager process.
Checklist
- give phase-cal-measure the offset in MHz and the right fs (245.76 TX/OBS; 30.72 or 61.44 RX)
- hint the ACTUAL tone frequency: the search covers only +/-30 bins (~+/-5.6 kHz)
  (a 325 kHz error on a 30.72 MHz capture returns "no tone / SNR 0")
- CW offset ~50-100 kHz: not ~100 Hz (DC bin), not tens of MHz (start-time error explodes)
- compare boards only inside one phase-cal-deltas run
Level 3 — repeatability, and the real judge: combining gain
Repeatability. RX deltas repeat within about 2°. In a 10-run regression the B1/B3 values moved by at most 4.2° and B41 RX by at most 1.8°. One B41 TX column reads dark, so dry-runs that include it are refused rather than committing garbage.

Why phase is judged by power. N equal paths combined coherently give 20·log10(N) of gain: 4 boards → 12.04 dB. Measured with the factory LUT: about 12.0–12.1 dB, i.e. essentially perfect. Any phase error θi reduces it to 20·log10(|Σejθi|): one board 90° off costs about 2.0 dB, one board 180° off costs 6 dB. So the total power at the antenna with all boards on (CST) is the end-to-end test of a calibration.
Case (one B3 column, TX)Power at antennavs zeroed LUT
Factory LUT52.73 dBm+1.28 dB
All offsets zero51.45 dBm—
Our commit51.94 dBm+0.49 dB (~40% of the factory improvement)
  • First real commit on B1: RX board spread fell from 118° to ≤16° and held. TX did not align (PHCAL01 open issue).
  • After commit, B41 RX matched the factory level within 0.1 dB on all four columns, but B1/B3 lost 0.6–2.1 dB versus factory — the loss is in the phases, not the amplitudes.
  • Low-band sign lesson: the low-band shifter moves the phase the opposite way. A commit therefore doubled the error and the factory values were restored. A sanity check against factory data reads about 0° when the sign agrees and about 180° when a board is flipped — run it before any commit on a new band.
Interview Q&A
Q: How does de-rotating and averaging extract the phase of a tone?
A: Multiplying by e^(−j2πfn/fs) cancels the tone's rotation, leaving a constant vector A·e^(jφ); noise keeps rotating and averages down by √N. The angle of the mean is φ.
Q: Why fit tone plus DC instead of taking a single DFT bin?
A: Off-bin, the finite-window tone basis is not orthogonal to DC, so LO leakage would leak into A and tilt φ. The 2×2 least-squares fit removes it.
Q: Three captures of the same tone give phases spread across the circle. Is the hardware drifting?
A: Probably not: absolute phase depends on capture start. At a 40 MHz offset one sample of arm jitter is ~59°. Use board differences under one held tone and a ~100 kHz offset.
Q: A spectrum shows the tone 34 dB above the floor, but the SNR gate rejects it. Why?
A: The gate uses per-sample SNR; per-bin height includes 10log10(nfft) of FFT gain (~36 dB at 4096). The tone is barely above the broadband noise; raise the level.
Q: How do you prove a phase calibration actually worked?
A: Measure combined power at the antenna with all boards on and compare factory, zeroed and new LUTs. Four coherent boards should give ~12 dB over one.
FPLAN01 RFSoC Frequency Planning — Fs, interpolation, Nyquist zones, NCO, DAC images, HD2/HD3 folding (with the N41 worked example) RCT click to expand ▾
In plain English
The RU's RFSoC converts directly between digital samples and RF: there is no analog mixer. That makes the sampling rate (Fs) the single most important number in the radio. It decides which Nyquist zone the carrier sits in, what the NCO must be set to, where the DAC images and folded harmonics land (and whether they hit someone else's band, or your own receiver), how much sinc droop you lose, and what rate DPD/CFR run at. Changing Fs ripples into four config files and every DPD NCO word. Frequency planning is the job of choosing Fs, interpolation and data-path mode for each variant so that all of this works for every carrier placement. ADC02 explains the converter physics; this card is the planning procedure, with the N41 study as the worked example.
One carrier, many copies
Every product k·Fc folds back into 0..Fs/2 and is mirrored by the image; the analog BPF has to stop whatever the sinc does not.
Level 1 — platform limits and the core formulas
Converters (ZU67DR RFSoC): DAC 2 tiles × 4 blocks, up to 9830.40 MS/s, and the blocks of one tile share Fs. ADC up to 2949.12 MS/s in quad mode, 5898.24 in dual mode. Valid rates are n × 245.76 MHz (plus 4300.80 = 17.5 × 245.76). There are 13 interpolation/decimation factors from 1 to 40 (not just 1/2/4/8), and P/Q resampling ratios of 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3, 7/2, 4 and 5.
Fs_DAC          = input_rate x P/Q x interp
DPD/CFR rate    = input_rate x P/Q                    (NR input_rate 491.52 MS/s)
Nyquist zone    NZ = ceil(Fc / (Fs/2))
NCO (general)   r = Fc mod Fs ;  NCO = Fs - r  if r > Fs/2  else r
first image     Fs - Fc
sinc droop      20 log10 | sin(pi Fc/Fs) / (pi Fc/Fs) |
harmonic fold   r = k Fc mod Fs ; mirrored to Fs - r if r > Fs/2
DPD NCO word    round(NCO / Fs_OBS x 2^48)
The NZ1/NZ2 shortcuts ("NCO = Fc" or "Fs − Fc") stop working from zone 3 upwards; the general mod form always works.
VariantDAC FsADC FsOBS Fs
B01039830.402949.125898.24
B416881.282949.124300.80
N789830.405898.241966.08
N415898.242949.122949.12
Usable band per DAC data-path mode: Bypass 0–0.45 Fs; IMR high-pass 0.3–0.45 Fs; IMR low-pass 0–0.2 Fs. IMR and Bypass have the same SFDR; IMR runs the DUC at half speed (less power, lower interpolation) but narrows the band. Prefer NZ1 + Bypass when it fits.
Level 2 — worked NCO examples and the planning checklist
B41 receive: ADC Fs 2949.12, Fc 2593. Fs/2 = 1474.56, so the carrier is in NZ2. r = 2593 (mod 2949.12) > Fs/2, so NCO = 2949.12 − 2593 = 356.12 MHz. rfdc-app may show either 2593 or 356.12 — both describe the same setting.
B41 transmit: DAC Fs 6881.28, Fs/2 = 3440.64 > 2593, so the carrier is in NZ1 and NCO = 2593 MHz. An older how-to called this zone 2 and also quoted −847.64 MHz (= −(Fs/2 − Fc)), an offset referenced to Fs/2 rather than DC; check which convention your tool displays before comparing numbers.

Checklist for every candidate Fs
1. carrier + BW/2 inside the usable band of the mode, for BOT, MID and TOP placements
2. images n*Fs +/- k*Fc for n = 0..3, k = 1..3: where do they land, and with how much sinc?
3. IM3 / IM5 between carriers (2CC)
4. HD2 / HD3 folds (DAC products, -53 to -81 dBc, NOT removed by interpolation)
5. FDD: does any image or harmonic fall in the unit's OWN receive band?
6. DPD/CFR rate = input x P/Q: does it change? then every DPD NCO word changes
7. verdict PASS / CONDITIONAL / FAIL, and write down WHY each reject was rejected
8. confirm the finalists in the vendor frequency-planner tool, then on the bench
Files a rate change touches: rfdc_config.json, nco_frequency.json, dpd_config.json and common.mk.
Level 2 — the N41 study (Fc placements 2516 / 2593 / 2670 MHz)
First correction: the signal is 40 MHz (2 × 20 MHz carriers); the 194 MHz of n41 (2496–2690) is the tuning range. Planning for 194 MHz of instantaneous bandwidth would rule out good options for no reason.
